sections.h2: When are Florida property taxes due and what discounts apply?
sections.html:
Tax collectors mail bills in November, and the Department of Revenue prints the early-payment discount as 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1.

Tax certificates are sold on unpaid accounts by June 1 (s. 197.343). Ask your county tax collector for the exact bill amount and any installment arrangement.

sections.h2: What does the Florida property tax calendar look like?
sections.html:
The year runs on a fixed cycle that starts January 1, the date the property appraiser assesses all property at just value. Most deadlines fall in the first quarter or in late summer.

Florida property tax cycle as printed by the Department of Revenue
TimingEvent
January 1Assessment date at just value
March 1Deadline to apply for exemptions and classifications
April 1Deadline for tangible personal property return (Form DR-405)
AugustTRIM notice (Form DR-474) mailed
September to NovemberBudget and millage hearings by taxing authorities
NovemberTax bills (Form DR-528) mailed
April 1 afterUnpaid taxes delinquent

A value challenge starts with a petition within 25 days of the TRIM notice. A denial of an exemption or classification has a 30-day window.

sections.h2: How does the Florida homestead exemption work?
sections.html:
A homeowner who lives in the property as a permanent residence on January 1 can claim up to $50,000 off assessed value (s. 196.031). The first $25,000 applies to all property taxes, including school taxes. The additional exemption of up to $25,000 applies to assessed value over $50,000 and only to non-school taxes, and it is adjusted each January 1 by the CPI change when that change is positive.

  • Apply with Form DR-501 to the county property appraiser by March 1.
  • The exemption is lost if the unit is rented, stops being the permanent home or the owner stops being a Florida permanent resident.
  • A servicemember may rent out the homestead without abandoning the exemption (s. 196.061).

sections.h2: What does the Save Our Homes cap limit?
sections.html:
After the first year of homestead and a just-value assessment, the assessed value of a homestead can rise each year by no more than the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, and it never exceeds just value (s. 193.155). Revenue's cap chart, revised January 2026, prints a 2024 cap of 3.0 percent, a 2025 cap of 2.9 percent and a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent.

Non-homestead property has its own limit: assessed value growth is capped at 10 percent each year. A sale, foreclosure or other transfer of legal or beneficial title is a change of ownership that resets the property to just value the following January 1, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses and certain transfers at death.

sections.h2: Can I carry my cap to a new Florida home?
sections.html:
Yes, through portability, if you establish the new homestead within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead was abandoned. The statute reduces the new home's assessed value by the lesser of $500,000 or the difference between the old home's just and assessed values (s. 193.155(8)). File Form DR-501T with the DR-501 by March 1.

The statute page notes that chapter 2026-239 amendments first apply to the 2027 ad valorem tax roll, so confirm current limits with the property appraiser.

sections.h2: Which senior, veteran and deferral benefits exist?
sections.html:
Several programs sit on top of the base exemption, and many depend on a local ordinance, so eligibility differs by county.

  • Age 65 or older: a county or city may allow an additional homestead exemption of up to $50,000 if household income is within the limit (s. 196.075(2)).
  • Veterans 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a discount equal to the VA disability percentage (s. 196.082).
  • Disabled ex-servicemembers rated 10 percent or more: a $5,000 reduction in assessed value (ss. 196.081, 196.091).
  • Deployed servicemembers: an exemption matching the share of the prior year deployed, claimed on Form DR-501M.
  • Tax deferral: file Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year.

Deferral covers the part of taxes above 5 percent of household income, or all of it if household income is under $10,000. A permanent resident aged 65 or older can defer the part above 3 percent of household income.

sections.h2: Who sets Florida property tax rates?
sections.html:
Taxing authorities such as counties, school boards, cities and special districts set millage rates at public hearings. They hold tentative budget hearings in September and October and final adoption hearings in October and November. State law also caps growth in a taxing authority's property tax revenue at Florida per capita personal income growth plus new construction, unless a super-majority, unanimous vote or referendum overrides it.

Look at the TRIM notice mailed in August for proposed millage, then check the tax collector's bill in November for the amounts levied.

sections.h2: What happens if Florida property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
The account becomes delinquent on April 1, and the tax collector sells a tax certificate to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps (s. 197.432). A certificate holder cannot contact the owner to demand payment until 2 years after April 1 of the year of issuance.

After that time, the holder may apply for a tax deed, with an application fee of $75 under s. 197.502. The clerk runs the public auction. On homestead property, the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value in addition to the amounts due. A high bidder pays a deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled when a Florida house sells?
sections.html:
Taxes are normally prorated at closing, and the title company will ask the tax collector for the current balance. Ask the collector for any delinquent amounts or certificates, and ask the property appraiser whether a homestead was removed after the sale.

Sellers should know the bill the buyer will face may be much higher, because the sale resets the property to just value the next January 1 and the Save Our Homes cap starts over.

faqs.q: When do Florida property tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: The tax collector mails them in November. Discounts of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent apply for payment in November, December, January and February.

faqs.q: When do Florida property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1 following the tax year. Tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: File Form DR-501 with the county property appraiser by March 1 of the tax year. You must make the property your permanent residence by January 1.

faqs.q: How much can a homestead's assessed value rise each year?
faqs.a: By the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change under Save Our Homes. Revenue's chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.

faqs.q: Can I defer my Florida property taxes?
faqs.a: Homestead owners can apply with Form DR-570 to the tax collector by March 31 after the assessment year. Deferral covers taxes above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.
